body: A paperback by Reiss Davies. The listing calls it his second book and gives its full title as The Ripple Effect: A Nu Flow.
The subject is water. The listing describes the book as looking at water in biology and in the world outside it, which is a description of a subject and not a claim about a reader.
A binding, an author, a title and a price. That is four things, and one of them is the price.
No page count, no ISBN, no publisher, no year, no page size, no language and nothing about illustration. Every one of those rows says not printed on the sheet below.

acc.summary: What this page does not say
body: The listing sets out what a reader is meant to get from the book. None of that is repeated here, in those words or in any others.
The listing carries its own note that the book is for educational and personal development purposes. That note is on the sheet below and the paragraphs above it are not.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: This is the thinnest sheet on the shelf, and that is the state of the listing today rather than a house habit. A page count and an ISBN are the two things any reader deserves before paying £33.00 for a book they cannot pick up first, and neither of them is printed.

reiss.label: From Reiss
reiss.h2: The second book, and a thinner sheet
paras: This one is a paperback and that is the whole of the physical description on the listing. No page count, no ISBN, no year. The other book prints 100 pages on its listing and this one prints nothing, and I would rather you saw that gap sitting on the sheet than did not notice it at the till.
The subject is water. What the book says about water is in the book, and moving any of it onto a shop page would turn an argument into a sales line, which is a different thing and a worse one.
reiss.pull: The subject is water. What the book says about it is in the book.
